text.p: London-based MC-BBL Securities rated both Hungarian oil and gas company MOL and gas distributor Primagaz as "hold" in its latest report.
"We maintain our 'hold' recommendation on technical grounds for both MOL and Primagaz," MC-BBL Securities analyst Stephen O'Sullivan told Reuters.
"(Primagaz shares) now look poised to break into a new high, although expect a volatile period," the report said.
According to Budapest Stock Exchange figures, Primagaz shares peaked at 11,400 forints on February 4 and closed at 11,175 forints, up 80 on Tuesday.

O'Sullivan said MOL shares could rise to 3,525 forints in the present rally but "resistance at the previous high may confine the shares to a trading range of 3,000 to 3,525 forints until a third attempt at breaking through 3,525 forints can be made".
On Tuesday, MOL shares closed at 3,020 forints, up 10.
